Yooka-Laylee studio explains upcoming Definitive Edition's absence on Xbox to 'frustrated' fans

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is notably skipping Xbox Series X/S consoles, and the studio blames "technical challenges and costs.".
  • The Definitive Edition is bringing support for 120fps, revamping the platformer's lighting, updating textures and shadows, and packaging in the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack DLC next month.
  • According to recent reports, "Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition is notably skipping Xbox Series X/S consoles, and the studio blames "technical challenges and costs.".

The Definitive Edition is bringing support for 120fps, revamping the platformer's lighting, updating textures and shadows, and packaging in the Trowzer's Top Tonic Pack DLC next month. But a large question mark hung over the lack of an Xbox version.

According to recent reports, "Hi folks, just wanted to say a massive thanks to everyone on here for the support for Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition. The response has BEE-n incredible, and we can't wait for you to experience the game all over again on December 15th," developer Playtonic Games said in a new social media post.

"We are aware of feedback regarding the lack of Xbox Series S/X support, and we just wanted to provide some clarity on the reasoning behind this decision. Bringing Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair: Definitive Edition to PlayStation 5 and Nintendo Switch 2 has been an exciting adventure… Unfortunately, we've had to prioritise our efforts given the technical challenges and costs presented in the creation of this updated version of the game and as a result, we are unable to commit to any additional platforms for the foreseeable future," it continued.

Playtonic remarked it understood Xbox players' frustrations, but the development costs associated with bringing the game to more platforms "just isn't viable for us at this time." Playtonic is still an independent game studio, after all, and Xbox console sales have been lagging behind the competition for quite a while.

Recent findings suggest that "As a small team, we hope you guys can understand the challenges we face. Please know that this wasn't an easy decision to make, and we apologise to any of you affected by this. We only wish things were different, and we value every single one of you and your feedback," the statement went on.

In a recent development, digital Foundry's John Linneman chimed in to tell folks that the omissions isn't a huge deal, because Yooka-Laylee and the Impossible Lair already looks pretty great on Xbox consoles. "The Xbox One X version of this game is already native 4K," he tweeted. "The upgrade seems minor, thus it's already excellent on Xbox. Was the best console version by far.".

The original Yooka-Laylee was a collectathon throwback in the same vein as Banjo-Kazooie, but this follow-up took more inspiration from Rare's Donkey Kong Country games instead - and the results were pretty stunning.

According to recent reports, "It's the upcoming in Impossible Lair which impresses, the tightness of the game's 2D controls and intricately designed levels which stands out, and which seems better fitted to Playtonic's toolbox," Eurogamer's review remarked. "It's a far more polished game than the studio's predecessor, and one well worth exploring through.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, prince William is reportedly actively considering a initiative for a “far-reaching restructuring” of the British monarchy, which he would implement once he ascends to the throne. His brother, Prince Harry, would be at the forefront of these changes: The future monarch reportedly wants only active members of the royal family who carry out duties on his behalf to retain their royal titles and the style of “Royal Highness.” These titles would therefore no longer be an “automatic privilege of birth” but would instead be equivalent to a “job title.”.

Industry observers note that the initiative was detailed by Tom Sykes, a journalist and writer specializing in the royals, in his book Dukes of Hazard, to be published next February, excerpts of which were published by the Mail on Sunday on Saturday, November 21. The author, “a royal authority with impeccable society contacts” as the newspaper puts it, is said to have obtained confessions from friends of Prince William.

“If you are a working royal—going out, touring the country, doing diplomatic work, doing government work, having a public role, pressing the flesh, getting out of bed on a wet Wednesday to go to Sheffield—then you will be an HRH and you will have a prince or princess title. You will also get an allowance, a salary, and a place to live. One place to live,” the associate of the prince explained to Sykes. “If you are not doing those things and you are not a working royal, you will not get to be an HRH, you will not get a free or subsidized place to live, and you will not get any special favors. You will, however, be a private citizen free to get on with your life and make money any way you choose.”.

Industry observers note that by implementing this measure, Prince William hopes to prevent potential media scandals regarding the legitimacy of certain individuals’ right to retain their titles if they are not prominent members of the Firm (Prince Harry) or if they are under legal scrutiny (Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor). But also, and above all, the Prince of Wales hopes to offer an option to his children, Princess Charlotte, 11, and Prince Louis, eight, who could easily renounce their titles to pursue independent careers. The question does not arise for the eldest child of the Prince and Princess of Wales, Prince George, 13, whose future as heir to the throne is “guaranteed.” In fact, none of the three use their royal titles, preferring simply to be called by their first names and the surname Wales.

Under the rules established by King George V in 1917, the title of prince or princess, along with the predicate, is granted at birth to the sovereign’s children and to the children of the sovereign’s sons, as well as to all the children of the Prince of Wales’s eldest son. Prince William’s children, therefore, received these titles at birth, while Prince Harry’s children, Archie and Lilibet (ages seven and five), did not become prince and princess until King Charles III ascended the throne.

In a recent development, they may have to give them up if Prince William carries out his plan. “Under William’s current plan, the prince and princess titles of Harry and Meghan’s children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, would be legally removed, along with the royal styles and princely titles of Harry and Meghan themselves,” writes Tom Sykes in his book. To do so, according to Sykes’s book, constitutional advisers have told William that he could concern letters patent, an official document authorized by the king. Such a decision could strain the relationship between the two brothers.

Sykes is convinced that Prince William would garner the approval of his subjects and “enormous public support in a country increasingly impatient with the cost and perceived excess of a sprawling royal household,” according to those close to him.

Sources indicate that in October 2025, Prince William confided to actor Eugene Levy—whom he was hosting at Windsor Castle for the taping of Levy’s show The Reluctant Traveler—that “there are points when you look at tradition and go, Is that still fit for purpose today? Is that still the right thing to do? Are we still doing and having the most impact we could be having?”.

Sources indicate that kensington Palace, however, declined to comment on the rumor. “As a matter of policy, we don’t comment on books or claims made within them.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Seemingly unperturbed by the criticism it faced after selling new Mass Effect merchandise following the shock closure of developer BioWare, EA is now flogging new merchandise for the studio's other big series, Dragon Age.

It has been revealed that EA's decision to close BioWare and cancel the long-awaited Mass Effect 5 in October was met with shock and condemnation from fans and games industry veterans alike. Legendary designer Warren Spector slammed the closure, and fan efforts to save the studio - including calls of support from Mass Effect voice acting talent - have continued in the aftermath.

Recent findings suggest that EA, apparently aware of the potentially poor optics, promptly scrubbed a number of Mass Effect-themed cosmetics from Battlefield, but eyebrows were raised when, just weeks later, fresh Mass Effect merchandise - including a $175 wearable LED helmet - was released onto its BioWare Gear store on 'N7' day, the annual celebration of BioWare's space series. Unsurprisingly, more criticism followed. As one fan put it at the time, "This is such a bad look".

And now here we are again. EA'S BioWare Gear store has sprung to life once more, this time (thanks IGN) to promote a new "Seven Swords of Nightmare" hoodie inspired by BioWare's Dragon Age: Inquisition.

"Unless you reopen BioWare, EA, then no money for you," one person wrote in a social media response indicative of the general sentiment from others. Some customers also used the opportunity to share the #savemasseffect hashtag beneath the BioWare Gear post - a related community initiative has so far seen over 330,000 fans sign a petition to save the series.

In a recent development, the community has been energised by glimpses of what could have been following Mass Effect 5's cancellation. At one point, a flashy internal trailer appeared online, and award-winning composer Austin Wintory also shared music he'd pitched for the game. Elsewhere, content creators claiming to have seen a work-in-progress version of Mass Effect 5 have called it "incredible" and claimed it would have drawn lessons from The Witcher and Baldur's Gate 3.

BioWare's closure in October came as part of the first round of layoffs at EA since the publisher's $55bn acquisition by a consortium including Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, investment firm Silver Lake, and private equity company Affinity Partners earlier this year. The move resulted in the loss of 400 jobs, with layoffs occurring across multiple studios, including Apex Legends developer Respawn, The Sims studio Maxis, and EA Motive.

Breaking: PS5s Are in Short Supply for Black Friday, but You Can Still Buy One

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (905 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There may be a ton of Black Friday deals on electronics, toys, and gadgets out there, but don't get your hopes up if you're looking for a PlayStation 5.
  • Sources indicate that whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers.
  • In a recent development, you still have some options for obtaining a PS5, but none of them are great.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There may be a ton of Black Friday deals on electronics, toys, and gadgets out there, but don't get your hopes up if you're looking for a PlayStation 5. Not only are they not discounted, but the combination of international chip shortages, high demand caused by the release of Grand Theft Auto 6, and the general holiday shopping frenzy has also made it nearly impossible to purchase a newly introduced, unbundled PlayStation 5 at any price—nearly impossible, but not impossible.

Sources indicate that whether you're looking for a PlayStation 5 Digital Edition, a PS5 with a disc drive, or the flagship PlayStation 5 Pro, you won't find them at major online retailers. PlayStation Direct lists all three consoles as "presently unavailable." Best Buy suggests making an account with them to "improve your odds" of getting one. I can't find a listing for a new PS5 on Amazon either.

In a recent development, you still have some options for obtaining a PS5, but none of them are great. Many refurbished PS5s are selling for well above the list price of a latest unit. There are some bundled, special editions available, but you'll likely be paying a ton for those. If you're willing to get your hands dirty by dealing with the wild west of Facebook Marketplace, you might be able to track down a used PlayStation 5 at a reasonable price, but approach with extreme caution.

If you're looking for a refurbished PlayStation 5, the best way to avoid a headache is to focus on who did the refurbishing. Buying refurbished electronics directly from a manufacturer is generally safer than buying from a third party, and in this case, it's cheaper too. PlayStation Direct is offering a "Certified Refurbished PlayStation 5 Console" for the relatively reasonable price of $519, while a refurbished Slim sells for $499. But if you're in the market, I'd lock it in quick: PlayStation Direct is already out of refurbished PS5 Pros.

In a recent development, amazon's Renewed program has some strict requirements for third parties to stay in the program, like keeping defect rates under 0.8%, but refurbished PlayStation 5s are going for a premium on Amazon at the moment. A quick look at the site reveals that the price of a refurbished PlayStation 5 is hovering near $900; a refurbished PS5 Slim will run you somewhere around $750, and the current average price of a refurbished PS5 Pro has ballooned to over $1,700. These are well above the retail prices of $649 for the standard version, $599 for the digital version, and $899 for the flagship Pro version of the PlayStation 5.

There are some bundled versions of the console listed for sale online too. If you buy one of these, you're getting a latest console and some other piece of hardware or a game, but there's a ton of upcharge at the moment. They're generally more expensive than the original price and more expensive than refurbished units as well. Here are some examples:.

Best Buy lists this PS5 Pro with PlayStation Portal Remote for $2,134.99.

GameStop lists a Ghost of Yotei Gold Limited Edition PS5 bundle for $769.99 ($731.49 for GameStop Pros).

Best Buy lists a PS5 Slim with an external drive for $979.99.

By far the largest used market for anything in the U.S. is Facebook Marketplace, including PlayStation 5s. I checked out my local Marketplace, and there are a lot of listings for the console within a 40-mile radius of Los Angeles. The average price of used PS5 consoles here is hovering between $300 and $500, which seems fairly reasonable. But with Facebook Marketplace, the number of potential red flags rises with the demand for the product.

I've bought and sold a fair number of things on Marketplace with no problems beyond the occasional flaky person, and I've written a list of hacks for the service, but I wasn't covering a "shortage buying" situation like this. Scams tend to rise with demand, so when I see a listing for a $150 PS5 console (that contains the text "$250 or best offer"), I'm suspicious. It could have been posted by someone who doesn't know what they have, but I wouldn't count on it. If you're buying a PS5 on Marketplace, check the model and generation details very carefully against the actual item. Make sure the seller is offering what you want and not a PlayStation 4 with PS5 games. Verify how it was stored and the condition it's in. But it ultimately can come down to vibes: Don't let your desire to score a PlayStation 5 get in the way of your gut check about the seller or situation.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Recent findings suggest that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a press pre-briefing ahead of the Devstream, Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford and community director Megan Everett discussed the scale of the Tau update, revealing just how much of an ambitious undertaking it's been for the team.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that warframe's latest devstream has just gone live, revealing more about the new Tau solar system players will be able to explore as part of December's "massive" new revision, which arrives on 9th December. Additions include a two-hour long quest, new explorable areas, and even chill nighttime dog walking.

In a press pre-briefing ahead of the Devstream, Warframe creative director Rebecca Ford and community director Megan Everett discussed the scale of the Tau update, revealing just how much of an ambitious undertaking it's been for the team. "This is a huge update, it is massive," Ford stated. "It is a second solar system ... Alone, by now, this would have been Warframe two. We're just going for it: we're building a new solar system brick-by-brick.".

That begins with a "two-hours-ish" story quest, according to Ford, but there's plenty more besides. Tau brings a latest navigation system, for instance, and will feature two playable regions at launch. The World-Seeder Oasis is one: full of environmental hazards, thanks to damaging terraforming efforts, and various missions to complete. Here, players can go bug-collecting for an NPC called Catulast. Doing so increases your standing with him, and provides new rewards.

Then there's the ringed city of Fornax. Unlike previous regions in Warframe, this features three hubs: the Lastbloom Lounge, Manifold 90-BF, and the Elder Rustgarden. All have their own playable missions, some brand-new and others returning from the original star system. This includes Spy, a returning mode that has players breaking into terminals while trying to remain undetected.

Spy hasn't been shown a lot of love for a while, and it seems like this upcoming iteration will bring new custom puzzles for players to take on. Ford notes it'll include codes to memorise, passwords to figure out, plus gameplay and an aesthetic that alights with the new Fornax setting.

Steel Path - the optional, more difficult variant of regular missions - also returns in Tau, although the Accolite mini-bosses who would hunt you down in previous Steel Path missions will not be present. Instead, the Hokra brothers will take that role: giant sentient casino goons who look quite daunting.

In a recent development, we were also shown more of the Last Bloom Lounge. Here you'll be given bounties that'll always bounce you between the three Fornax hubs. So, if you take one bounty in the Lounge, you'll complete it while out on a mission, and end up in either Manifold or the Rustgarden (which is still being kept secret for now). That way you'll be naturally circling between the three locations.

Sources indicate that however, rather than there being three separate syndicate reputations to grind out, one single syndicate connects them all: the Fornax Informer, a newspaper run by kids obsessed with breaking stories across the ringed city. Print lives! By progressing through the ranks with this syndicate, you'll unlock clues for detective work that reveal a special cinematic within the Lounge, though this too is being kept secret for now.

By completing bounties, you'll also gain access to Fornax's own progression system which provides still-mysterious buffs and other beneficial effects within Tau. There's also a card game in the Lounge, which you can either play against the house or with other players.

Recent findings suggest that as for navigating between the hubs, each one has its own garage. The Tau patch comes with a driving minigame: an on-rails opportunity to gather resources and fend off other drivers along the way. In the demo shown, we're brought from the Lounge to the Manifold, dodging barriers and blowing up other sentient vehicles in the process. There's also a "low stakes, no combat" way to navigate between the hubs. It's called Night Walk, a first-person dog walking mode where you can travel.

It's wild to think about but Survivor has been on the air for 26 years now. The competition series (which is streaming with a Paramount+ subscription) started its run back in 2000, and longtime fans are still up to date with the current Season 51. A lot has changed over the years, including Survivor's prize money, the amount of days the game lasts, and how casting works. I recently watched a vintage clip from back in Season 2, and it totally made me miss OG Jeff Probst.

The second season of the show was titled Australian Outback, and is arguably one of the best Survivor seasons in the show's long history. Some of the most iconic players ever came out of Season 2, including Jerri Manthey and the great Colby Donaldson. I recently saw a clip of a wildly dangerous challenge, and I was shook by how different the entire show feels nowadays. You can check out the video for yourself below:.

A post shared by Susie Mac (@survivordeepdive).

In a recent development, honestly, how crazy is this Survivor challenge? Rather than the standard ones we're used to seeing every season, the above clip highlights Jeff asking the cast to jump off a cliff and try to survive floating down rapids with boxes of supplies. It's truly terrifying to watch it play out, especially when you consider that Rodger Bingham had only JUST learned to swim before starting the game.

I loved re-watching this unique challenge, as I've grown tired of seeing the same ones every single season. I mean, how many times can we watch the contestants do the same puzzle? The show's early seasons used to have challenges that were themed based on their location, making each one unique. Although as we know, Survivor has been permanently based in Fiji since Season 33. So the location-based theming has been gone since 2016.

Industry observers note that seeing this retro Survivor clip also made me miss the OG version of host Jeff Probst. While he's pretty warm and cuddly nowadays, he used to be more of a hard ass. I used to love hearing him throw shade at the contestants, often adding salt to fresh wounds in the process. Seriously, he used to call people or tribes "completely useless" back in the day. This always cracked me up, but nowadays the host/showrunner is more likely to give folks a warm hug.

Jeff used to be scary during classic Survivor, but that's simply not the vibe anymore. I mean, castaways are so comfortable around him they're willing to interrupt his speeches and even give him a nickname like "Uncle Jeff." Where's the respect, people?

Survivor airs latest episodes Wednesdays as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see if Probst ends up changing his tune at all throughout the rest of Season 51.

Latest Update: Junk bonds are 'flashing yellow.' Watch these warning signs

📅 09 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1038 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt.
  • High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago.
  • The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cracks are forming in the junk bond market as investors demand higher payouts for owning the market's riskiest debt. It isn't time to ditch high-yield bonds, but investors should pay attention to the warning signs.

High-yield bonds now yield 8.1%, up from 7.22% a month ago. The increase reflects a jump in yields across the curve as investors bake in more inflation from high energy prices and other pressures, including concern about the deficit — hitting nearly $2 trillion in the fiscal year that ended Sept. 30.

The high-yield market is also showing stress on the credit side with spreads recently widening to levels not seen since April, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. Credit spreads are the difference in yield between the bonds and Treasurys of similar maturities. Wider spreads mean investors are demanding higher yields for holding corporate debt, viewing it as riskier.

Recent findings suggest that spreads are at 315 basis points in the overall high-yield market, higher than a year ago but still below levels in March when they reached 346 bps. One basis point equals one one-hundredth of a percent, or 0.01%.

In a recent development, the high-yield market consists of bonds rated BB+ by S&P and Fitch and Ba1 and under by Moody's. The lowest-rated cohort, CCC and below, has seen the most movement with spreads climbing dramatically over the past year to roughly 1,250 bps.

Right now, the high-yield market is "flashing yellow" but is "far from red," said Michael Arone, chief investment strategist at State Street Investment Management.

It makes sense that investors are demanding more compensation for taking on additional credit risk as borrowing costs rise, he said.

Yields are elevated across the board with the 10-year Treasury reaching its highest level since 2002 earlier in the week.

"The bigger question is whether this is simply a repricing of interest rate risk, or the beginning of a more fundamental reassessment of credit quality," Arone said.

He's in a wait-and-see mode since earnings are still growing, interest-coverage ratios remain good, and while default rates have ticked up some, he believes it is not concerning.

That said, the starting point in spreads is likely weighing on investors' psyche, since they are still low by historical standards.

It has been revealed that "There's a small margin of error here, which I also think raises the anxiety level," Arone explained. "The compensation that investors are receiving for taking on this credit risk isn't overwhelming relative to history, and therefore subtle changes in credit spreads can be concerning.".

While there may be concerns about part of the lower-rated market, the overall high-yield market is in good fundamental shape.

In fact, credit quality is at a record high, with BB bonds making up over 60% of the market compared with 38% prior to the global financial crisis, said Kelley Gerrity, a fixed income strategist at Morgan Stanley Investment Management.

In a recent development, "We've had higher-quality companies coming in, and with higher rates now, you also have more discipline from companies that are more indebted ... just because of the higher cost of capital, so that actually is creating a bit of a healthier picture as well," she said.

Recent findings suggest that the lowest tier of high yield has always been more speculative, since the bonds have a higher default risk. Therefore, it's no surprise that they are the ones seeing the most widening in spreads, remarked Collin Martin, head of fixed income research and strategy at the Schwab Center for Financial Research.

In a recent development, the overall move in high-yield spreads have been "orderly," he mentioned. "Are there cracks forming? I think the cracks are logical cracks with the lowest-rated bonds and it's too early to say that it's spreading to the broad credit market.".

Recent findings suggest that in addition, fluctuations within the CCC-rated and lower spreads have been idiosyncratic, Gerrity added. Morgan Stanley recently broke down the spreads in the lowest cohort into two buckets: performing assets and non-performing assets, which are defined as spreads above 1,000 bps.

The non-performing spread to worst is 2,818 bps, while the performing bucket — the biggest piece of the CCC market — is 461 bps, she said.

Recent findings suggest that "It is isolated," she noted. "I'm not necessarily sure that that will go away anytime soon, but it doesn't tell the story of overall concern and flashing caution for credit markets right now.".

For now, investors should remain selective within higher yield, Gerrity advised.

"We're looking for the best relative value opportunities, and we think that exists within that single-B cohort, and so we're leaning into that," she noted.

Investors should be concerned if there is a steep widening in the broader high-yield market.

But there's scant evidence of stress in the BB cohort. Spreads in that group are at 194 bps, up from 179 bps a year ago — although the move hasn't been in a straight line.

In a recent development, "We're going to be focusing our attention on what are considered some stronger businesses," Martin remarked. "If we start to see the markets demand higher spreads there also, that's what we'll be looking at to see if risks are really rising.".

It's also vital to understand that the Federal Reserve is raising rates in a strong economic environment, mentioned R.J. Gallo, chief investment officer of global fixed income at Federated Hermes. The central bank is concerned about an inflation problem amid high fossil fuel prices due to the Iran war, while growth has been stronger than expected, he noted.

"With growth being good as the reason that the Fed is hiking, then you wouldn't expect high yield to blow out because growth means revenues stay up, means cash flow and profitability stays up," he explained.

High yield becomes a disaster when the economy is heading into a sharp economic downturn, Gallo said.

According to recent reports, "That's when spreads really widen out," he noted. "But a recession is not the odds-on bet. Now, talk to me in six months if the Fed keeps hiking over and over, if oil prices stay high for longer, well, then maybe we will start to wonder.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in 2021, at the recommendation of a film producer, the writer and showrunner Rebecca Cutter read a pulpy murder-mystery novel on a flight from her native Massachusetts to her current base in Los Angeles. By the time she landed, Cutter had finished the book and was already mapping out the TV adaptation in her head.

In a recent development, the plot heavily involved a Texas abortion clinic, and the state had just passed SB 8, one of the country’s most restrictive abortion bills until Roe v. Wade was overturned the following year. As she contemplated bringing The Hunting Wives to life, Cutter saw the political stakes come into focus as well.

Sources indicate that “I started thinking about the ‘red state, blue state’ of it,” she tells Vanity Fair ahead of the show’s season two premiere on Thursday. “What if…we really play this culture war?”.

It has been revealed that “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes,” claims showrunner Rebecca Cutter. “I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.”.

The result was one of Netflix’s biggest breakout hits in recent years, sent up in a Saturday Night Live sketch as the “straight but lesbian, horny Republican murder drama.” As a show, Hunting Wives amps up the noirish aspects of the suspense thriller written by May Cobb, a native of the East Texas Piney Woods, and adds a heaping dose of MAGA-adjacent camp. Cutter finishes the mix with plenty of sex scenes, particularly between Malin Akerman’s Margo, a femme fatale partly inspired by Melania Trump who is married to a Republican gubernatorial hopeful, and Brittany Snow’s Sophie, a liberal do-gooder who, like Cutter, arrives in town from a blue corner of Massachusetts. (Cutter was raised in Cambridge and graduated from Wesleyan University, the Connecticut liberal arts college known for its progressive politics and pipeline to Hollywood.).

Hunting Wives executive producer Erwin Stoff told Cutter he’d pay for her to go to Texas to meet Cobb and breathe the Piney Woods air herself. She met Cobb’s father and her best friend from high school. She shot skeet with the women—she even got it in three, just as Sophie does in the first season. At a high-end Dallas shopping area where the likes of Gucci can be found, Cutter got a better sense of the hair, clothes, and bodies of her eventual characters. “I understand the notion that Sophie could be amused and entertained and intrigued by these women,” Cutter indicates, “and eventually seduced.”.

According to recent reports, cutter thinks of the show primarily in terms of its tonal mash-up: “I think we managed to wrangle it into one piece of art,” she claims, “but there’s comedy, there’s violence, there’s noir, there’s soap, there’s earnest emotion.” To the extent that she assigned any political beliefs to the rich white women of Cobb’s novel, it was in the spirit of grounding her characters in the specifics of their world. Still, as we speak, Cutter decides “to get real with it.”.

Recent findings suggest that cutter on set. She describes Sophie, a fellow native of blue Massachusetts, as a surrogate for her own awakening to MAGA Texas.

“The whole thing was a little bit of a parable, in my mind, of how you could fall for someone like [Donald] Trump,” she admits. “Sophie has her principles, but they only go so far. They end right where something starts to make her feel good.” Cutter was as curious as anyone else from her educated milieu about the quirkier aspects of Trump, like the Diet Coke button he had installed on the Resolute Desk. How liberating must it feel to embrace a movement so openly untethered from the pieties of politics and taste?

“Not that my show is a deep dive on Trump,” Cutter notes, “but maybe there is an element that’s sort of looking under the hood.”.

The twisted love story between Margo and Sophie entangles all of the wealthy, hard-drinking, gun-toting women in their orbit, and its central killing—one of several propelling the show forward, with a third season slated to begin filming this year—stems from an effort to cover up Margo’s abortion as her NRA-loving husband plots his political ascent. (In this proudly oversexed town, he has his own share of affairs.) Hunting Wives is the rare Netflix soap to receive steady coverage from mainstream national outlets; the fascination undoubtedly has something to do with the impression that, like Yellowstone or Morgan Wallen before it, the show unlocks something about MAGA’s cultural staying power. In a Latest York Times guest essay this month that evaluated the post-2024 Hollywood landscape, Sharon Waxman, the editor in chief of The Wrap, wrote, “From Melania on Amazon’s streaming service to The Hunting Wives on Netflix to the ever-expanding Taylor Sheridan universe on Paramount+ to Bari Weiss’s being put in charge of CBS News, the vibe shift was visible on all our screens.”.

Margo and her politically ambitious husband are partners in subterfuge and debauchery.

It has been revealed that cutter claims she had no particular agenda nor any “ultra-evil villain plan of how it was going to be received or how it would be culturally relevant.” But Hunting Wives is sprinkled with enough proper nouns—a Peter Thiel mention here, a Walmart reference there—and distinctly modern aesthetics that she can acknowledge its appeal as something of a Rosetta stone for the moment in MAGA femininity. Even in the ostensibly waning days of the movement, the plastic surgery and soaring heels continue to captivate and horrify coastal elites. Cutter says that Callie (Jaime Ray Newman), another of Margo’s lovers, has a bit of Kristi Noem and Marjorie Taylor Greene in her: that “sort of slightly butch, real gun, real ‘back the blue’ [element]…the toughness of those women.”.

It has been revealed that the second season of Hunting Wives maintains the slipperiness that keeps the show from veering into moralism; it stands apart from other Trump-era art in its refusal to take sides. “I think I remember, in the pitch, someone saying, ‘But will red-state people like it too?’” Cutter recalls. “I was like, ‘I think so.’” Both Margo and Sophie are awash in their respective red and blue stereotypes, but neither is more admirable than the other. Their sordid union is a testament to the flexibility of both their principles and their preferences. From one vantage, it is, in the end, all about sex.

Recent findings suggest that “Margo is the symbol of freedom and sexuality and feminine power and empoweredness and selfishness that [Sophie] feels she’s lost,” Cutter says, adding that Akerman’s comfort in such a role helped drive her liberal use of physical intimacy. “The audience may disagree with me,” she says, but “I don’t think I do gratuitous sex scenes. I think you always are seeing a power dynamic play out or a plot point play out.” Last year, though, when Netflix acquired Hunting Wives, which was initially ordered by Starz in 2023, Cutter had a more practical concern.

“I literally googled,” she recalls, “‘Does Netflix show boobs?’”.

I've used a Blue Yeti for nearly a decade and it would happily serve for a decade more. A classic design, good hardware controls, and zero fuss. It's not for true audiophiles, but its quality and affordability are still hard to match all these years later.

Key specs: USB A | Four pickup patterns | Hardware gain control.

Blue Yeti price check: Best Buy $69.99 | Walmart $69.99.

The Blue Yeti might be the most popular USB microphone ever made, and you know what, it earned it. At its usual price, this is a great USB microphone. At $69.99 (its lowest price ever), it's simply one of the best bangs for your buck in this category.

The original Blue Yeti released in 2009, and in 17 years it has barely changed. I've had mine for a decade, and as I look around, I'm realizing it is the longest-lasting gadget on my desk. That's because it just works: I plug in, adjust the gain, and my voice comes through clear.

These days there are more advanced microphones than the Yeti, like its official sequel the Yeti 2, and certainly mics that are just as competitively priced. Those are good too, and I encourage you to check out cheaper options (like the $26 Amazon Basics mic that we surprisingly love) before making any decisions.

According to recent reports, but with the Yeti, you absolutely get what it says on the tin. I also think it's still an attractive mic, but it is quite large, so make sure it'll fit on your desk without blocking the corner of your monitor. I've had mine on a mic arm for the past few years, and while it does feel like I'm cosplaying a podcaster just to chill with friends on Discord, it's very convenient.

Sources indicate that at this price, it's firmly on the high end of "budget" territory while still sounding as good as mics that cost twice as much. If you do use it for long sessions and prefer to keep your mic open, play with the gain levels and make sure software noise cancelling is on in your chat app of choice (Discord's is pretty good out of the box).

If that's not enough, consider pairing it with dedicated noise cancelling software like Nvidia Broadcast (assuming your GPU can handle the extra toll).

As Christmas inches closer, fans are getting more into the spirit thanks to the 2026 Christmas movie schedule. Hallmark once again offers a large variety of classics and has over two dozen newly introduced holiday films this year. A massive number of people have already been watching Countdown to Christmas. However, the network’s beloved lineup does not just include the main channel. Hallmark’s Christmas classics have also made their way to Hallmark+. I love the holiday films, and there are two great ones that you can only watch on streaming, for the most part, that is.

Get Hallmark+ for just $2.99 a month.

Get in on this Black Friday deal through Amazon to save massive on your first three months and watch all the best Christmas and other holiday movies the streamer has to offer. Including movies that are only available on Hallmark+.

As previously mentioned, there are a handful of originals exclusively for Hallmark+, such as the When Calls the Heart prequel Hope Valley: 1874, which is coming back for Season 2. This includes the four-movie Unwrapping Christmas collection that premiered back in November 2024. Even though they premiered two years ago, the movies definitely still hold up, and two of them are arguably the best in the series.

In a recent development, unwrapping Christmas follows four friends working at a gift-wrapping shop leading up to the town’s Christmas gala. Similar to The Wedding Veil series, each movie centers on a different friend and their Christmas romance. The first one, Unwrapping Christmas: Tina’s Miracle, stars Natalie Hall as the titular Tina Mitchell, the owner of mentioned gift-wrapping shop. She finds herself in a bind after the Christmas gala she’s planning is nearly canceled until she teams up with an estate tech giant owner to save the venue.

Of course, Hallmark is no stranger to plots about saving a business or building in time for the holidays. And the network has been criticized for being too formulaic. That being said, Tina’s Miracle is still a great watch because it sets up the rest of the movies and her own love life. She’s hesitant to open up because of a past breakup, but ultimately, she and Michael (Alec Santos) team up to save the historic venue Alford House. With some twists and turns included, it’s perfect.

The second and third movies, Mia’s Prince with Kathryn Davis and Lily’s Destiny with Ashley Newbrough, are definitely fun watches and can get anyone into the spirit. However, I do love the fourth movie, Olivia’s Reunion, which sees gift-wrapping expert Olivia (Cindy Busby) getting snowed in with her ex while delivering gifts ahead of the gala. I am a sucker for a good enemies-to-lovers plot, especially if stated enemies were previously together. Putting the characters in a closed space for an undisclosed amount of time, you never know what could happen. Plus, Jake Epstein, who plays the ex, has a soft spot in my heart after portraying Craig Manning on Degrassi: The Next Generation.

It has been revealed that all four Unwrapping Christmas movies ultimately premiered on Hallmark Channel in July 2025, but seeing that they are Hallmark+ exclusives, I couldn’t help but relive them. Fans can relive those movies and plenty more Hallmark favorites on Hallmark+. Countdown to Christmas is far from over, and there is a movie for everyone.

Sources indicate that in the mood for a little bloodsport? In GTA 6, you can teach one loud-mouthed hunter that Lucia (or Jason) is the deadliest game, as this secret mission will require cunning and sharp shooting to survive. It's Hard Target meets SAW, and the victor gets a pretty sizable stack of cash. Here's how you can be the most elusive of quarry. Go to Hyde Island Located north of Lummox County and the Moreau River, Hyde Island is where you can start this mission. All you have to do is land on the island, and after a few steps, a dart will hit you and knock you out. Listen to your captor's speech Now for the boring part. You'll wake up inside of a shipping container, with a fashionable explosive necklace locked in place. Once your captor finishes his rant, the game begins, and you'll want to move. Run to the tent directly in front of you You'll have 10 seconds to reach a tent in front of you, where you'll find a gun and a paltry two rounds for the sidearm. After the count is up, a hunter on a quad bike will show up, and he'll be gunning for you. To make things worse, he also has a dog with him that'll track you throughout the island. Don't engage him; he's heavily armored, and two bullets aren't nearly enough to stop him—besides, you'll need those rounds for his dog, Caesar. Sorry, animal lovers. Search for more outposts You can find more ammo, adrenaline, and a shotgun at nearby outposts. Each one is lit up, so be fast, be sneaky, and try not to get caught. The hunter is going to be tracking you constantly, even without his dog, and he has a sniper rifle that can take you out in just a few shots if he catches you. Prepare for a showdown Get as much ammo as you can, and choose your spot for the last stand. The hunter's dog will be a pest, so deal with it first. It's easy to spot, with a red light on its collar. Trees also make for good cover against the hunter, so once he's in range, start nailing him with shots to critical areas. Once he stumbles, unload a few shotgun rounds and finish him off. Collect your rewards Once the hunter is down, search his body for the Island-Poacher FF-50 sniper rifle and ammo for it. Head west to the boathouse to reclaim your personal items and $15,000 in cash. Not a bad haul for a deadly night's work. What happens if you fail? If the hunter does kill you, you'll lose a chunk of cash and wake up near one of your safehouses. The good news is you can retry the mission by heading back to Hyde Island, but the bad news is you'll have to listen to the hunter's speech again.
